title: Medical Director, MD Pediatric Neurology
description:
**Who We Are:**
---------------

Neurocrine Biosciences is a leading biopharmaceutical company with a simple purpose: to relieve suffering for people with great needs. We are dedicated to discovering, developing and commercializing life-changing treatments for patients with under-addressed neurological, psychiatric, endocrine and immunological disorders. The company's diverse portfolio includes FDA-approved treatments for tardive dyskinesia, chorea associated with Huntington's disease, classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome, endometriosis\* and uterine fibroids\*, as well as a robust pipeline including multiple compounds in mid- to late-phase clinical development across our core therapeutic areas. For more than three decades, we have applied our unique insight into neuroscience and the interconnections between brain and body systems to treat complex conditions. We relentlessly pursue medicines to ease the burden of debilitating diseases and disorders, because you deserve brave science. For more information, visit neurocrine.com, and follow the company on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and YouTube. (*\*in collaboration with AbbVie*)

  
At Neurocrine, strong leadership drives both business results and team success. We look for leaders who think strategically, anticipate what’s ahead and set clear direction, while building and empowering high-performing teams. Successful leaders foster an environment where people are motivated to do their best work and deliver meaningful, measurable impact through sound decision-making and accountability.

**About the Role:**
-------------------

Responsible for the development of clinical research strategies and independent direction of Phase 1-3 clinical studies while working with a cross-functional project teams (clinical project managers, preclinical/clinical pharmacology, biometrics, regulatory, drug safety). May work closely with Research and Preclinical Development to develop biomarkers necessary for the most effective evaluation of novel molecules in early clinical development. Responsible for medical oversight of Drug Safety activities in conjunction with operational activities of the Drug Safety Director. Partners with Business Development in the assessment of external innovation.

\_

**Your Contributions (include, but are not limited to):**
---------------------------------------------------------

* Develops and implements study protocols as in conjunction with a multidisciplinary Development Team.
* Assist in the identification and selection of clinical investigators for clinical trials and maintain appropriate communication and professional relationships as Sponsor medical monitor/representative
* Conduct medical assessment and disposition of adverse events (in conjunction with Drug Safety physician) and evaluate safety of clinical compounds prior to and during ongoing clinical studies;
* Oversee the clinical trials program in conjunction with Clinical Operations in accordance with NBI SOPs, Good Clinical Practice, and applicable regulations.
* Analyze, interpret, and present results of clinical studies to internal and external audiences as directed by Sr. Management;
* Identify resource requirements, assist in budget planning and personnel forecasting for clinical research programs;
* Assists in the recruitment, training and development of the clinical teams.
* Identify and select clinical consultants.
* Provide or assist in the scientific writing and review of clinical study reports and related regulatory documents;
* Provides periodic status updates and effectively communicates with Senior Management Team.
* Leads the development of clinical biomarker strategies for early clinical development.
* Assist in the recruitment, training and development of the clinical teams;
* Identify and select clinical consultants;
* Work with Medical Affairs and external opinion leaders to secure new collaborators and present trial results;
* Identify resource requirements, assist in budget planning and personnel forecasting for clinical research programs;
* Interface with Research, Product Development and Business Development to assess new product opportunities, develop clinical research strategy and product development plans;
* Other duties as assigned.

**Requirements:**
-----------------

* MD or DO degree with accredited residency training and board certification in relevant clinical specialty for the therapeutic area required AND 2+ years of experience in clinical research and development (Phase 1-4) in either a pharmaceutical/biotechnology company or a clinical research/academic environment or related experience required.
* Knowledgeable in Good Clinical Practice, regulatory procedures relevant to investigational drug development
* Strong knowledge in translational medicine and biomarker evaluation, clinical study execution, regulatory requirements and documents, study design, biostatistics, data analysis, report writing, and scientific presentation of data
* Able to effectively operate in a multi-level matrix corporate environment, requiring interaction with, and/or direction of clinical research project teams, including physicians, scientists, monitors, administrative, regulatory, commercial, and consultant personnel
* Demonstrated success managing interactions with external CROs, consultants and other contract organizations, especially from the context of a small group.
* Proven track record of success across all phases of drug development, proven success record in clinical trial design
* Recognized as an internal thought leader with extensive technical and business expertise within a strategic organization
* Applies in-depth knowledge of own function, business / commercial / scientific expertise to solve critical issues successfully and innovatively
* Evaluates key business / scientific challenges and completes complex, ambiguous initiatives having cross-functional impact
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills as well as strong organizational and team leadership skills are required
* Able to work independently and prioritize multiple tasks and goals to ensure the timely, on-target and within-budget accomplishment

#LI-KM1

Neurocrine Biosciences is an EEO/Disability/Vets employer.

We are committed to building a workplace of belonging, respect, and empowerment, and we recognize there are a variety of ways to meet our requirements. We are looking for the best candidate for the job and encourage you to apply even if your experience or qualifications don’t line up to exactly what we have outlined in the job description.

\_

The annual base salary we reasonably expect to pay is $254,600.00-$347,000.00. Individual pay decisions depend on various factors, such as primary work location, complexity and responsibility of role, job duties/requirements, and relevant experience and skills. In addition, this position offers an annual bonus with a target of 35% of the earned base salary and eligibility to participate in our equity based long term incentive program. Benefits offered include a retirement savings plan (with company match), paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage in accordance with the terms and conditions of the applicable plans.

title: Lab Research Technician - Bader Lab
description:
National Jewish Health is seeking a **Lab Research Technician** to join the Bader Laboratory in the Department of Immunology and Genomic Medicine. Reporting to Jackie E. Bader, PhD, this entry-level position supports research investigating how obesity influences immune cell function and impacts anti-tumor immune responses. The Laboratory Technician will assist with laboratory experiments, data collection, and daily laboratory operations while contributing to a newly established research program focused on immunology, cancer biology, and metabolic disease.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Perform routine laboratory procedures and experiments under the direction of the Principal Investigator.
* Assist with primary immune cell isolation, flow cytometry, and other laboratory techniques used to support ongoing research studies.
* Collect, record, organize, and assist with the analysis of research data.
* Maintain accurate laboratory records, samples, and research documentation.
* Support laboratory operations, including inventory management, supply organization, equipment maintenance, and mouse colony activities.
* Adhere to laboratory, animal care, and institutional safety standards and requirements.
* Collaborate with research team members to advance multiple ongoing projects.

National Jewish Health is the nation's leading respiratory hospital and a world-renowned center for immunology and biomedical research. This position offers an exciting opportunity to join a newly launched laboratory and gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge immunology research while contributing to discoveries that may improve the understanding and treatment of cancer and metabolic disease.

  

**Position Summary:** The position performs as an entry-level technician under the direction of a Principal Investigator or Laboratory Manager, which may include assisting in collecting, tabulating and analyzing research data.

  

**Essential Duties**

* Performs routine laboratory tests under the direction of a Principal Investigator or Lab Manager.
* Collects, accurately records and analyzes data in conjunction with other research staff.
* Obtains and maintains minimum proficiency in data analysis, preparation of glassware, extraction and plating procedures, basic programming and mathematical ordering systems. May utilize computer.
* Maintains compliance with all institutional/safety training requirements.
* Maintains laboratory records, supplies and samples in an organized manner (such as a laboratory notebook and sample storage record).

  

**Core Values**

* Be available to work as scheduled and report to work on time.
* Be willing to accept supervision and work well with others.
* Be well groomed, appropriately for your role and wear ID Badge visibly.
* Be in compliance with all departmental and institutional policies, the Employee Handbook, Code of Conduct and completes NetLearning by due date annually.
* Promotes a workplace culture based on mutual respect and merit, where all individuals are treated fairly and provided with equal opportunity to contribute to the mission and goals of the institution.
* Adheres to safe working practices and at all times follows all institutional and departmental safety policies and procedures.
* Wears appropriate PPE as outlined by the infection control policies and procedures.
* Demonstrates compliance with all state, federal and all other regulatory agency requirements.

  

**Other Duties**

* Performs all other duties as assigned.

  

**Key Competencies**

* **Laboratory Knowledge:** Demonstrates and understands laboratory testing and methodology.
* **Decision Quality:** Makes good decisions based upon a mixture of analysis, wisdom, experience, and judgement. Sought out by others for advice and solutions.
* **Adaptability:** Maintains effectiveness in the midst of change in work responsibilities or environment, requirements ambiguity, or stress.
* **Problem Solving:** Uses issue identification, data relation and comparison, pattern recognition and information gathering to create analyses and make recommendations.
* **Informing/Communicating:** Conveys ideas, responses, or instructions effectively, appropriately, and persuasively through writing or speech.
* **Professional Relationships:** Interacts with others in a constructive, positive, and respectful manner, regardless of individual differences. Assists team members or co-workers in achieving personal goals and completing assignments.

  

**Minimum Qualifications**

* **Education:** Bachelor's Degree required.
* **Work Experience:** None
* **Special Training, Certification and Licensure:** A demonstrated basic knowledge of laboratory procedures, laboratory equipment, and data collection /classification required.

  

**Salary Range:** $22.76 - $30.10

  

**Benefits**  
At National Jewish Health, we recognize that our outstanding faculty and staff are the essence of our organization. For every aspect of health care, our employees are our greatest asset. With that in mind, we have designed a valuable, comprehensive benefits package to meet the needs of our employees and their families.

* **Comprehensive Medical Coverage:** Multiple Cigna health plans for Colorado, regional office and remote employees. Health Savings Accounts (HSA) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) available to pair with some plans.
* **Paid Time Off:** Generous PTO accruals to use for vacation and sick days, and six paid holidays, all compliant with Colorado state sick leave regulations.
* **Dental & Vision Plans:** Coverage effective the first of the month after hire.
* **Retirement Savings:** 403(b) plan with employer contributions after two years.
* **Wellness Incentives:** Earn up to $200 annually for preventive health activities.
* **Tuition Reimbursement:** Up to $5,250 annually for full-time and part-time employees.
* **Child Care Assistance:** Childcare Flex Spending Account (FSA) with annual employer contribution.
* **Loan Forgiveness:** Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) eligible employer.
* **Disability & Life Insurance:** Employer-paid plans and optional buy-up choices.
* **Voluntary Benefits:** Full suite of coverage options such as Accident, Hospital Indemnity and Legal Plan
* **Exclusive Discounts:** Savings on local services, insurance, and RTD bus passes.

title: Scientific Program Manager
description:
**Overview**

Scientific Program Manager

Job Type: Full-time

Location: Hybrid (United States); Colorado residence preferred

Salary: $80,000–$110,000 per year, depending on qualifications and experience

Travel: Occasional, approximately 15% or less

Reports to: Chief Operating Officer (COO)

K5 Biosciences, LLC (K5B) is a new, independent medical research organization focused on supporting philanthropic efforts to accelerate scientific discoveries and advance innovative therapies for patients affected by rare diseases.

K5B brings together leading investigators, academic medical centers, biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, healthcare systems, and patient advocacy organizations to tackle some of the most challenging problems in rare disease research.

K5B will support a flagship initiative focused on C3 glomerulopathy (C3G), a rare kidney disease driven by dysregulation of the complement system. Through this initiative, K5B aims to establish an integrated discovery and therapeutic development platform combining patient registries, centralized and federated biobanks, large-scale multimodal datasets, international research networks, and clinical trials designed to accelerate the translation of scientific discoveries into effective therapies.

Importantly, the C3G program is envisioned not only as a means to accelerate progress against this specific disease, but also as a discovery platform for broader applications in autoimmunity, complement-driven diseases, rare kidney disorders, and transplant medicine. Insights, technologies, research infrastructure, and therapeutic strategies developed through the C3G program may be extended to related conditions that share underlying immunological and molecular mechanisms.

**Position Summary**

K5B is seeking an enthusiastic, scientifically trained, and highly organized Scientific Program Manager to help establish and coordinate an ambitious portfolio of biomedical research initiatives and strategic partnerships.

Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, the Scientific Program Manager will play a central role in coordinating collaborations with leading universities, academic medical centers, biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, and international research organizations.

The initial priority will be supporting the C3G research program, including the development of collaborative research networks, patient registries, biobanking infrastructure, multimodal datasets, and clinical research initiatives. The Scientific Program Manager will also help coordinate the expansion of these capabilities into related research programs in autoimmunity, complement-mediated disorders, rare kidney diseases, and transplant medicine.

The successful candidate will work at the intersection of scientific discovery, research operations, and strategic partnerships, helping translate ambitious scientific goals into coordinated research programs and measurable outcomes.

This position offers a unique opportunity to join a new biomedical research organization during its formative stages, work flexibly across a broad portfolio of activities, and develop and grow your position in scientific program management in collaboration with organizational leadership.

**Key Responsibilities**

*Program and Collaboration Management*

· Coordinate scientific collaborations involving academic institutions, biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, healthcare systems, nonprofit research organizations, and patient advocacy organizations.

· Support the development, implementation, and ongoing management of collaborative research agreements, sponsored research agreements, data-sharing agreements, and other scientific partnerships.

· Work with leadership and external collaborators to define project objectives, milestones, timelines, budgets, and deliverables.

· Organize scientific working groups, conferences, investigator meetings, steering committees, and project reviews.

· Monitor progress across multiple research initiatives, prepare progress reports, and help resolve operational challenges.

· Facilitate communication and coordination among scientific investigators, clinical researchers, industry partners, institutional leadership, and scientific and technology vendors.

· Help develop project management tools, tracking systems, and reporting processes to support an expanding research portfolio.

*Translational and Clinical Research Programs*

· Support the development and coordination of disease-specific patient registries, natural history studies, longitudinal research cohorts, and clinical trials.

· Coordinate collaborations involving centralized and federated biobanking networks, including biospecimen collection, processing, storage, and sharing.

· Facilitate initiatives integrating clinical data, electronic health records (EHR), patient-reported outcomes, and molecular profiling datasets.

· Help coordinate the generation and integration of large-scale multimodal datasets, including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and other advanced technologies.

· Work with scientific and technical teams to support standardized research protocols, data harmonization, quality control, and responsible data sharing.

· Support activities related to clinical study planning, site engagement, study feasibility, and operational readiness.

*Scientific Communications and Strategic Initiatives*

· Prepare scientific presentations, executive summaries, research progress reports, and briefing materials for leadership and external partners.

· Assist with the preparation of collaborative research proposals, funding applications, manuscripts, and scientific program documents.

· Contribute to strategic planning discussions and identification of emerging research opportunities.

· Help develop and maintain documentation of research programs, partnerships, and accomplishments.

**Required Qualifications**

· PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in biomedical sciences, biology, genetics, immunology, pharmacology, biochemistry, clinical research, or a related discipline; or

· Master's degree in one of these fields and at least four years of relevant experience; or

· Bachelor's degree in one of these fields and at least six years of relevant experience.

· Strong understanding of biomedical research processes and the scientific research environment and interest in rare disease research, translational science, and therapeutic development.

· Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to coordinate multiple concurrent projects.

· Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with scientists, clinicians, and external collaborators.

· Ability to work independently, establish priorities, solve problems, and meet deadlines in fast-paced, evolving, start-up environments.

Prior experience in scientific program management is not required for PhD-level applicants. PhD graduates interested in starting a career in program management are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Preferred Qualifications**

· Scientific background or research experience in nephrology, complement biology, autoimmune diseases, or organ transplant.

· Familiarity with clinical research, patient registries, biobanking, clinical data systems, or multi-omics technologies.

· Experience preparing scientific manuscripts, grant applications, research proposals, or technical reports.

· Familiarity with multi-institutional research collaborations, academic-industry partnerships, research agreements, or sponsored research programs.

**Career Development and Growth Opportunities**

K5B is committed to supporting the professional development of its team members.

The Scientific Program Manager will gain direct exposure to the development and operation of a new biomedical research organization, including strategic scientific partnerships, research infrastructure, clinical research networks, and collaborations with academic and industry leaders.

As the organization grows, successful candidates may have opportunities to assume different or increasing responsibilities, manage larger scientific portfolios, supervise additional team members, and advance into more senior positions, depending on performance, organizational needs, and available opportunities.

The position offers opportunities for mentorship from senior scientific and operational leadership and professional development through participation in national and international scientific initiatives.

**Location and Travel**

This is a hybrid position based in Aurora, CO. The organization has a strong preference for candidates residing in Colorado, where key organizational activities and collaborations will be based. However, qualified candidates residing outside Colorado may be considered.

Occasional domestic and potentially international travel will be required for scientific meetings, research collaborations, conferences, and other activities. Travel is expected to represent approximately 15% or less of working time.

**Compensation**

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is $80,000–$110,000, depending on education, relevant experience, qualifications, and responsibilities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; 401(k) retirement plan with employer contributions; paid time off and paid sick leave; paid holidays.

**Why Join Us?**

· Join a new, philanthropically supported biomedical research organization at an exciting stage of its development.

· Help establish a flagship C3G research program designed to generate discoveries and research capabilities with applications across multiple rare and immune-mediated diseases.

· Work with leading investigators, academic institutions, biotechnology companies, and pharmaceutical partners.

· Gain experience across multiple dimensions of biomedical research, from molecular discovery and patient registries to clinical trials and therapeutic development.

· Work directly with organizational leadership and contribute to strategic scientific initiatives.

· Benefit from flexible work arrangements, professional development opportunities, and a clear potential career advancement pathway.

· Make a meaningful contribution to improving the lives of patients and families affected by rare diseases.

**How to Apply**

Interested candidates should submit:

· A current curriculum vitae or résumé.

· A brief cover letter describing their scientific background, relevant skills, and interest in the role.

Candidates may be asked to provide professional references during later stages of the selection process.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. There is no application deadline.

K5B is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and supportive research environment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration in accordance with applicable employment laws.

Colorado residents: In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

Pay: $80,000.00 - $110,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Employee discount
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Parental leave
* Relocation assistance
* Retirement plan
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance
